title: SCH-CNT-002 standard encounter schedule
description: The standard encounter schedule. The project-owned typed validator in src/MechaMiner.Content/Categories/ remains authoritative; this schema is the draft 2020-12 mirror kept for editor and tool interoperability, and a fixture corpus proves the two reach the same accept/reject verdict on every structural case. See content/schemas/README.md. An aggregate: players never read its name and it is not embodied in the world, so it omits name_key and presentation_id.

id.title: A stable, case-sensitive ASCII content ID

mode.description: The run mode this schedule governs.

duration_minutes.description: How many minutes the run lasts. The minute-row array's length is checked against this rather than against a constant, so raising one without the other fails.

minimum.derivation: the section makes integer currency and rank values integral in source; a count of things that exist begins at one, because a count of zero is the absence of the field rather than a value of it

boss_arrival_warning_seconds.description: How long before a boss arrives the warning fires. The schedule owns arrival timing, so this value lives here once instead of in four places.

minimum.derivation: the section states that durations are nonnegative and that rates cannot be negative, so the floor of every duration and rate is zero and there is no upper bound the section supplies

population_ceilings.description: Three ceilings and the rule for exceeding them.

min.description: The floor of the reduction band.

minimum.derivation: the section scopes _percent to human-readable percentage points; the floor of a share of a whole is zero of them, which is the share that is none of it

maximum.derivation: the section scopes _percent to human-readable percentage points; the ceiling of a share of a whole is one hundred of them, which is the whole, and a larger value is not a share of anything

spawn_formations.description: Every formation the schedule defines. Each appears exactly once, so a minute row can never name a formation the schedule has not defined.

formation.description: One of the seven accepted spawn formations.

minItems.derivation: the grammar names seven formations and this block defines each of them once, so the floor is the vocabulary's size; a shorter array would leave a formation the grammar names undefined

maxItems.derivation: the same vocabulary size as the floor; a longer array would either define a formation the grammar does not name or define one of them twice

phase_pressure_curve.description: The authored intent the minute rows implement.

minute_rows.description: One row per minute of the run, in minute order.

hyper_gold_beacon_response.title: The Hyper Gold beacon response table
hyper_gold_beacon_response.description: The schedule is the single writer on what each response is; the site keeps only the progress thresholds at which its beacon fires.

trigger_rule.description: What triggers the four response packages.

population_symbol.description: What the population symbol in the table means.

elite_exclusion_enemy_id.description: The enemy excluded from beacon elites.

version.title: A positive integer version
version.description: The initial schema_version and content_version of every first-authored definition is 1.

minimum.derivation: the initial value of every first-authored definition is 1 and both versions only ever increment, so no valid version is below 1; there is no upper bound because a definition may be revised without limit

name_key.title: Localization key for the player-facing name

summary_key.title: Localization key for the concise player-facing summary

tags.title: Closed query and tooling vocabulary
tags.description: The vocabulary starts empty, so [] is the only accepted value.

presentation_id.title: Logical presentation entry
presentation_id.description: Omitted when a definition never appears in-world. No accepted document mints a grammar for a presentation ID, and inventing one for a category with zero members would be structure ahead of need, so the only constraint is that an authored value is not the empty string.

minLength.rationale: not a capacity bound: the empty string is what the compiler materializes for an omitted field, so an authored empty string would be a second way to say 'absent'. 1 is the smallest length that excludes it

minute_row.title: A minute row
minute_row.description: One minute of the standard schedule.

minute.description: The minute this row governs. Compared against the row's array index, so a gap, a repeat, and a reordering all fail.

minimum.derivation: the section makes counts integral; this one is summed into a report column across the catalog, so zero is authored rather than omitted and the floor is zero rather than one

authored_event_or_boundary.description: The authored cell for this minute.

batch_count.description: How many enemies one pulse places.

interval_seconds.description: The interval between pulses. Strictly positive: a zero interval is a single instantaneous placement of the whole minute's population rather than a pulse rate.

exclusiveMinimum.derivation: the section makes durations nonnegative and rates non-negative; this quantity is additionally one the definition divides by, scales by, or spends, so zero is excluded as well and the bound is exclusive rather than inclusive

composition.description: The weighted identities selected for baseline replenishment. The shares of one row sum to one hundred; the sum is over the row and not the schedule.

share_percent.description: This enemy's share of the row's replenishment.

minimum.derivation: a share expressed in percentage points; zero would be the absence of the entry rather than a value of it, so the floor is the smallest share that is not that, which is one point

maximum.derivation: a share expressed in percentage points; one hundred of them is the whole, and a share cannot exceed the thing it is a share of

debut_enemy_ids.description: The enemies that first appear this minute.

formation_events.description: The authored formations layered over replenishment this minute.

authored_cell_text.description: The schedule table cell, kept because one row's timestamps were reconstructed and the original token has to stay legible.

items.description: One of the seven accepted spawn formations.

timestamp_provenance.description: Whether these timestamps are authored or reconstructed. A consumer that trusts them without reading this is reading provisional numbers as accepted ones.

boss_arrival_boss_id.description: The boss arriving this minute. The timecode is the boss definition's; the warning timecode is derived from boss_arrival_warning_seconds.

beacon_response.title: A beacon response package
beacon_response.description: One row of the response table.

trigger_progress_percent.description: The crossing this package fires at.

minimum.derivation: a crossing strictly inside the extraction; zero is the activation trigger rather than a crossing, so the floor is the first whole point after it

maximum.derivation: a crossing strictly inside the extraction; one hundred is completion rather than a crossing, so the ceiling is the last whole point before it

floor_count.description: The minimum response size. This and share_percent are the two operands of the response size, which is the larger of them; they replace an authored expression string that restated both.
